title: Machine-learning-assisted design predicts Netsene, a 3D carbon nodal-surface semimetal
summary: A theory-guided inverse-design study combined a crystal diffusion variational autoencoder with a Crystal Transformer to propose a body-centered tetragonal C24 allotrope, Netsene. First-principles calculations report dynamical and mechanical stability and a nested nodal-surface semimetal band structure with drumhead surface states. This is a computationally predicted allotrope and electronic phase, not an experimentally synthesized material.
ai_technology: Crystal diffusion variational autoencoder (CDVAE) and Crystal Transformer, guided by symmetry-engineering theory
organization: Authors’ institutions include Nanjing University and associated materials-physics groups (see arXiv record)

evidence.tested: A theory-guided inverse-design study combined a crystal diffusion variational autoencoder with a Crystal Transformer to propose a body-centered tetragonal C24 allotrope, Netsene.
evidence.unknown: The allotrope and its properties are computational predictions validated by first-principles calculations; the paper does not report synthesis or experimental observation. The finding is one proposed material/phase result from one paper, not a claim that AI alone established the physical existence of Netsene.
evidence.ai_role: Generated and ranked candidate crystal structures within a theory-guided inverse-design workflow; the resulting Netsene structure was then assessed with first-principles calculations for stability and topological band properties.
